title: NetCrafter: Tailoring Network Traffic for Non-Uniform Bandwidth Multi-GPU Systems
problem: Hierarchical multi-GPU systems connect GPU groups with high-bandwidth intra-group links but lower-bandwidth inter-group links, creating severe performance bottlenecks on the inter-group network when traffic is not carefully managed. Conventional GPU communication treats all network flits uniformly, leaving bandwidth partially unutilized while also generating unnecessary traffic.
motivation: As ML workloads require ever more GPUs, hierarchical non-uniform bandwidth interconnects are the practical scaling path, but the resulting bandwidth imbalance between intra- and inter-group links creates disproportionate performance degradation at the slower inter-group fabric.
method: NetCrafter applies three techniques at the network boundary to manage traffic on the lower-bandwidth links connecting GPU groups. It packs together partially-filled packets (network data units called flits) heading to the same destination to maximize bandwidth usage, drops speculative prefetch requests that haven't been requested to eliminate wasted traffic, and reorders packets so time-critical data reaches its destination before bulk data. These techniques reduce delays for critical requests without modifying the GPU compute pipelines.
key_novelty: NetCrafter combines three traffic-shaping techniques—packet packing, filtering of unused speculative requests, and priority-based reordering—to exploit the unequal bandwidth structure of hierarchical multi-GPU systems.
contributions: Identification of three distinct inefficiency classes in hierarchical multi-GPU network traffic: partial flit utilization, unnecessary speculative fetches, and latency-insensitive flit ordering.
Flit stitching mechanism that coalesces compatible partially-filled flits to recover wasted bandwidth.
Flit trimming mechanism that drops speculative flits not yet demanded, reducing inter-group traffic volume.
Flit sequencing mechanism that prioritizes latency-sensitive flits, reducing effective access latency for critical data.
